title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events — where you went, what you saw and did — using Pashto's split-ergative past tense.
intro:
This is the most important grammar unit in the course. Pashto is **split-ergative**: in the present, sentences work like English ('I eat the bread'), but in the past, **transitive** verbs switch to a different pattern — literally 'by me the bread was eaten'. The doer goes into the oblique case, and the verb agrees **with the object**, not the subject.

Intransitive verbs ('go', 'come', 'arrive', 'become') stay simple and agree with their subject. So the first question for every past sentence is: does this verb have an object?

vocab.note: Present stem وين-: وينم wínəm. Past: ما وليد / وليده 'I saw (him / her)'.
f. تېره. تېره اوونۍ 'last week', تېر کال 'last year'.
Perfective: تېر کړم. Past: ما ښه وخت تېر کړ.
Past: زه وزېږېدم 'I was born'. Also پيدا کېدل.
پيدا کول 'to find', پيدا کېدل 'to be found; be born'.
f. ورکه. ورک کول 'to lose', ورک کېدل 'to get lost'.
Usually: هېر مې شو 'I forgot (it)' (lit. it became forgotten to me).
m. ياد مې دی 'I remember'; ياد مې شوې 'I missed you'.
m · pl: خبرونه 'the news'. خبر يم 'I know (about it)'.
m. په پای کې 'in the end'.
m. اتڼ کول 'to dance the attan'.

grammar.title: Intransitive past: like English
grammar.body:
Verbs **without an object** (go, come, arrive, sit, become …) form the past simply: past stem + endings, agreeing with the **subject**:

زه لاړم lā́ṛəm · ته لاړې lā́ṛe · هغه لاړ lāṛ (m) / لاړه lā́ṛa (f)
موږ لاړو lā́ṛu · تاسو لاړئ lā́ṛəy · هغوی لاړل lā́ṛəl

Notice the 3rd person: masculine singular often has **no ending** (or -ə), feminine **-a**, masculine plural **-əl**, feminine plural **-e**.

The **perfective** past ('I went', with stress on the first syllable or on wə́-) is the normal past for completed events. The **imperfective** past ('I was going', stress on the ending) uses the imperfective stem: تلم tlə́m 'I was going', پاڅېدم 'I was getting up'.

Key irregulars: تلل → **لاړم**; راتلل → **راغلم** (هغه راغی m / راغله f); کېدل → **شوم** (هغه شو m / شوه f).

grammar.title: Transitive past: the ergative construction
grammar.body:
With verbs that **have an object** (see, eat, do, buy, read, say …), the past tense works differently:
1. The **doer** goes into the **oblique** case: زه → **ما**, ته → **تا**, هغه → **هغه** (m) / **هغې** (f), سړی → **سړي**, ښځه → **ښځې**. (موږ، تاسو، هغوی don't change.)
2. The **object** stays in the **direct** case.
3. The **verb agrees with the object** in gender and number.

So with خوړل 'eat':
ما کباب **وخوړ** 'I ate the kebab' (کباب m sg)
ما ډوډۍ **وخوړه** 'I ate the bread' (f sg)
ما مڼې **وخوړې** 'I ate the apples' (f pl)
ما وريجې وخوړې · ما کبابونه **وخوړل** (m pl)

This leads to sentences that look 'back-to-front' to English speakers: **هغه زه وليدم** 'he saw me' — هغه is the oblique doer, زه is the direct-case object, and the verb ends in -əm because it agrees with زه!

If there's no explicit object, the verb takes the masculine plural form: هغه وويل چې … 'he said that …'.

examples.en: He saw me. (lit. by him I was seen)

grammar.title: Clitics as the doer, and 'have done'
grammar.body:
In the past, the clitics **مې دې يې مو** often replace ما / تا / هغه as the **doer** of a transitive verb — this is extremely common in speech:

ډوډۍ **مې** وخوړه 'I ate the bread' (= ما ډوډۍ وخوړه)
کتاب **يې** ولوست 'he/she read the book'
څه **دې** وکړل؟ 'what did you do?'

The **present perfect** ('I have seen') uses the past participle in **-ay / -e / -i** + 'to be', and it also follows the ergative rule — the participle and the 'be' verb agree with the object:
ما کابل **ليدلی دی** 'I have seen Kabul' (کابل m)
ما دا فلم نه دی ليدلی 'I haven't seen this film'
زه هلته **تللی يم** 'I have been there' (intransitive: agrees with زه).

dialogue.title: The wedding last week
dialogue.setting: Shirin tells her friend Hila about her cousin's wedding in the village.

lines.speaker: Hila
lines.en: Shirin, where were you last week?

lines.speaker: Shirin
lines.native: کلي ته لاړم، زما د تره د زوی واده و.
lines.roman: kə́li ta lā́ṛəm, zmā də trə də zoy wādə́ wə.
lines.en: I went to the village — it was my cousin's wedding.

lines.speaker: Shirin
lines.native: ډېر ښه و! ټوله کورنۍ راغلې وه. ډېر خلک مو وليدل.
lines.roman: ḍer ṣə wə! ṭóla kornə́y rāġə́le wa. ḍer xálək mo wə́lidəl.
lines.en: It was wonderful! The whole family had come. We saw lots of people.

lines.speaker: Hila
lines.en: Did the men dance the attan?

lines.speaker: Shirin
lines.native: هو، ټوله شپه يې اتڼ وکړ! ښځو هم سندرې وويلې.
lines.roman: ho, ṭóla shpa ye aṭáṇ wə́kaṛ! ṣədzó ham sandə́re wə́wayəle.
lines.en: Yes, they danced the attan all night! The women sang songs too.

lines.speaker: Shirin
lines.native: پرون ورسېدم. په لار کې ناڅاپه زموږ موټر خراب شو!
lines.roman: parún wə́rasedəm. pə lār ke nātsā́pa zmuẓ moṭár xarā́b shu!
lines.en: I arrived yesterday. On the way our car suddenly broke down!

lines.speaker: Hila
lines.en: Oh no! Then what did you do?

lines.speaker: Shirin
lines.native: زما ورور يو مستري پيدا کړ، او دوه ساعته وروسته روان شوو.
lines.roman: zmā wror yaw mistrí paydā́ kaṛ, aw dwa sāʿáta wrústa rawā́n shwu.
lines.en: My brother found a mechanic, and two hours later we were on our way.

culture: The **attan** (اتڼ) is the national dance of Afghanistan and of Pashtuns everywhere: dancers move in a circle to the beat of the dhol drum and the surnai, spinning faster and faster, their long hair and scarves flying. It is danced at weddings, Eid and national celebrations. Pashtun weddings last several days, with separate gatherings for men and women, music, and a huge feast — مېلمستيا, hospitality on the grandest scale. Note the grammar in 'my brother found a mechanic' above: زما ورور looks like the direct case, but masculine nouns ending in a consonant often have no visible oblique ending — the verb کړ agrees with the mechanic.

tip.title: The past of go, come, arrive
tip.body:
- Verbs with no object take endings for the **subject**, as in English: زه لاړ**م** · ته لاړ**ې** · موږ لاړ**و** · هغوی لاړ**ل**.
- 'He' often has no ending, 'she' adds **-a**: هغه راغی / هغه راغل**ه**.
- 'Was': زه **وم** · ته **وې** · هغه **و** (m) / **وه** (f).

tip.title: Past with an object: ما وليد
tip.body:
- With verbs that take an object (see, eat, buy), the doer changes: زه → **ما**، ته → **تا**، هغه → هغه / **هغې** (f).
- The verb agrees with the **object**, not the doer: ما کباب وخوړ (m) · ما ډوډۍ وخوړ**ه** (f) · ما مڼې وخوړ**ې** (pl).
- موږ، تاسو، هغوی don't change.
tip.pattern: ما + object + past verb (agrees with the object)

lessons.title: I lost it, I forgot, I remember

tip.title: مې as the doer, and 'have done'
tip.body:
- In speech the doer is often a clitic: کتاب **مې** ولوست 'I read the book', ډوډۍ **دې** وخوړه؟ 'did you eat?', **يې** 'he/she'.
- 'Have done': participle + 'to be', agreeing with the object: ما کتاب **لوستلی دی**.
- 'I forgot' = هېر مې شو (lit. it became forgotten to me).
tip.pattern: کتاب مې ولوست · کتاب مې لوستلی دی
